etymologies.etymologyHTML: From motive +‎ -ate (verb-forming suffix). Compare French motiver.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To provide someone with an incentive to do something; to encourage; to actuate.

quote.citation: 2021 March 10, Drachinifel, 17:51 from the start, in Guadalcanal Campaign - The Big Night Battle: Night 1 (IJN 3(?) : 2 USN)‎[1], archived from the original on 17 October 2022:
quote.text: Armor-piercing shells were heading up the shell hoists, but this procedure took a few minutes, allowing the battered American flagship to reply in kind, the gunners somewhat motivated to set new records for the rate of fire as the cruiser raked the larger ship from stem to stern in response.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To animate; to propel; to cause to take action.
